questions.question: (a) Vehicle for the '0.33 is frozen' rule (BK-512)? Context: RFC-0025 already amends RFC-0024's D2, D8, D9, R2, R3 class K, R4, R5 while master's code is 0.33 (release/0.33.x retired, patches tagged from master). Every earlier change to RFC-0024 came as its own RFC plus an 'Amended by' line (0025 to 0029).

options.label: New RFC-0031 (Recommended)
options.description: Short RFC amending RFC-0024 (Summary, D8, R3 class K, R4, R5) and RFC-0025's rows for them, with Alternatives and the decision logs. RFC-0024 and RFC-0025 each get an 'Amended by RFC-0031' line; their text stays as history. Rule 3, principle 5 and the agent copy point at it.

options.label: Amendment line in RFC-0024
options.description: RFC-0024 gains an 'Amended 2026-11-04 (BK-512)' Status line and its K/R4/R5/D8 sentences are rewritten in place. No new file, but RFC-0025's rows on the same clauses then amend text that changed under them, and the rejected options live only in the decision log.

questions.question: (b) What does a difference between v1 and 0.33, found by spec/observe work, become?

options.label: Evidence, then a break row (Recommended)
options.description: Found during spec/observe work: recorded as evidence in that flow's research report, as BK-511 § 7 does. At D8's comparison: a v1-breaks.md row when the v1 clause differs from what 0.33 does, else nothing. Never a BK/BUG item against 0.33, even when 0.33 also breaks its own spec.

options.label: Break row as soon as found
options.description: A v1-breaks.md row at discovery, before D8. Rows then exist without a v1 clause ID (R5's 'v1 clause' field empty until the spec lands), and D8 re-checks them.

options.label: Evidence plus a users' note
options.description: As the first option, and a known-0.33-gaps list in the user docs so callers learn of them without a filed item. Adds a docs page to keep in step with the evidence.

questions.question: (c) Does the 0.33 line still take a fix for a user-reported issue, and who rates it a patch? (Today: patches tag from master; the first v1 change to src/ cuts release/0.33.x, RFC-0025 D5.)

options.label: Yes, maintainer rates (Recommended)
options.description: A user-reported issue may become a 0.33 BUG; its fix ships in a 0.33 patch (from master now, as a cherry-pick to release/0.33.x after the cut) only if CONTRIBUTING's bump table rates it patch, and the maintainer confirms that rating when admitting the item. Otherwise it is a candidate break for its flow.

options.label: Yes, bump table alone
options.description: Same, but the author applies the bump table and the PR review checks it; no separate maintainer admission step.

options.label: No further 0.33 fixes
options.description: 0.33 takes only security and patch-eligible floor fixes; a user report becomes D8 evidence or a break row and is fixed in 1.0.0. CONTRIBUTING § Release and R3 class K say so.

BUG-341, BUG-342, BUG-343 (older K items, not user-reported) stay as they are: the rule covers new items.

options.label: Move it, and the older K items
options.description: As the first, plus BUG-341, BUG-342 and BUG-343 leave the backlog as D8 evidence too, so no open item treats 0.33 as a fix target. Wider sweep; reverses fixes RFC-0024/0025 rated patch.

options.label: Keep as a 0.33 BUG
options.description: Grandfathered: filed before the rule, stays open as a K item, fixed as a 0.33 patch. The rule applies only from BK-512 on.

RFC-0031 (PR #1207, unmerged) says /observe sessions, reviews and spikes "find" 0.33 differences, which treats the leak as normal. RFC-0024 R1 and the ground register say 0.33 is never ground; only D8's comparison, after the spec, reads 0.33. How should RFC-0031 state it?

options.label: Design half never reads 0.33 (Recommended)
options.description: F2 says it outright, citing RFC-0024 R1 and the ground register: design, review, spike and spec never read 0.33's code, tests or specs, so they find no 0.33 differences; only D8 reads 0.33. F1 drops 'observe, spike' from its list. Anything about 0.33 that already exists (BK-511 § 7, BUG-346) is D8 input only.

options.label: Also cut F2's evidence step
options.description: As above, and F2 keeps only D8's comparison. BK-511 § 7 and BUG-346 are described as records made before this rule, not as a step anyone takes. Shorter, with no evidence stage at all.

questions.question: Two places still let design work use 0.33 code: /observe SKILL.md:73 lets a reopen item cite a check on 0.33's code as a witness of SDK/OS behaviour, and the OP-01 spike ran its checks against LocalBackend (0.33 code). Fix these in PR #1207 too?

options.description: SKILL.md:73: an SDK or OS behaviour is witnessed by a probe of the SDK or OS itself, never through 0.33's code. RFC-0031 adds: a spike checks a record against a reference model or the raw SDK/OS, never a 0.33 backend. Process-budget bytes may need a recorded raise.
